Align.description: The nine alignment keywords, used to place content inside its frame.

Asset.description: A file the collection carries with it.

path.description: Relative to the collection root, always.

Audio.description:
Whether the item's source is heard. A source is audible when any live item
of it says so, which is OBS's behaviour and changes no pad topology.

oneOf.description: Heard while the item is visible on programme.
Heard whether the item is visible or not.

Blend.description: OBS's blend enum, so an import carries across unchanged.

Canvas.description:
The output raster. One per collection in this release; 11 section 1 leaves
room for several.

anyOf.description: A source id: a slug, because an operator types it.

Another scene in this collection, with sparse overrides keyed by the
target's item id (USD's `over`, Godot's revertable override). Unity
keys overrides by array position and silently attaches them to the
wrong entry when the source changes.
A graphic template, by its plugin qualified id.

Content.description:
What an item shows.

A group is an item whose content is an inline list of children: no special
type and no special rules. OBS made a group a modified scene and collected a
decade of transform corruption bugs (2913, 4173, 5478, 9297, 9298, 9558).

Crop.description:
How much of the content's own pixels to trim, normalised 0 to 1 so it
survives a canvas change. vMix and CasparCG do this; OBS crops in pixels,
which is why an OBS collection moved from 1080p to 720p loses its crops.

Filter.description: One filter in an item's chain.

type.description: The plugin qualified provide id, for example `chroma/filter`.

Fit.description:
How content fills its frame. SVG's vocabulary, which replaces OBS's seven
bounds types and maps onto `sizing-policy` on a `glvideomixer` pad.

oneOf.description: The content's own size, scaled by `scale`. The frame is ignored.
Fit inside the frame, keeping the aspect ratio.
Fill the frame, keeping the aspect ratio, cropping the overflow.
Fill the frame exactly, distorting the aspect ratio.
Scale so the width matches; the height falls where it falls.
Scale so the height matches; the width falls where it falls.
Like `contain`, but never scale up past the content's own size.

Frame.description: The rectangle an item is fitted into.

Id.description: A UUID in the hyphenated form. Minted ids are version 7 (time ordered); ids derived from a layout are version 8.

Item.description:
One placement of content in a scene. Not a "layer": the code already uses
that word for the superimposed page.

bind.description:
Layout bindings: a geometry path such as `frame.w` against a small
arithmetic expression over the layout's params and `W`, `H`. Present
only in a layout preset; `layout::apply` resolves them and leaves this
empty on the scene it produces.

filters.description:
Filters belong to the item, not to the source. OBS attaches them to
sources only, so a camera keyed in one scene is keyed in all of them and
the workaround is a nested scene per placement.

order.description:
Where this item sits among its siblings. See `Scene::order`: the same
key, for the same reason, and what makes a drag one record on the wire.

Override.description: A sparse change to one item of a referenced scene.

Scene.description: A named, ordered composition of items on the canvas.

color.description:
A free colour for every client, the tally and the Stream Deck to agree
on (11 section 6b). Absent means the client picks one by kind.

items.description: Bottom of the stack first, the way the compositor takes them.

order.description:
Where this scene sits among its siblings, as a sort key rather than an
array index. Stored so that inserting a scene changes one key on the
wire instead of renumbering every other one; assigned by
`Collection::renumber_order` when it is missing, so a document written
by hand or by an older build needs nothing.

SourceMeta.description: A source's name, colour and tray folder, as this collection has them.

color.description:
Free text so a client can use whatever it draws with. Absent means the
client picks one by kind.

group.description:
A tray folder: a tag on the source, purely for finding things. Not a
scene group, which is a thing on the canvas.

Transform.description: Where an item sits and how it is sized.

anchor.description:
Normalised 0 to 1 within the item's own box: (0,0) top left, (0.5,0.5)
centre, (1,1) bottom right.

frame.description:
The rectangle the content is fitted into, in canvas pixels. Absent
means the content's own size, scaled.

position.description: Canvas pixels, of the item's anchor point.

Transition.description: A named transition between two scenes.

Vec2.description: A point or a pair of factors.

description: A GodwinMix scene collection: canvas, parameters, scenes of items, transitions and assets. See docs/reference/scene-document.md.

assets.description:
Assets by id, each a path relative to the collection root with a hash.
Never an absolute path: OBS stores those, which is why every commercial
scene bundle ships a relink wizard.

params.description:
A JSON Schema block in OGraf's manifest shape, readable on its own
without fetching values, so an agent discovers what is fillable before
filling it. `{{name}}` in a string prop binds to a property here.

sources.description:
What this collection calls the sources it refers to: a name, a colour
and a tray folder each (11 section 6b). Not a source list, which the
mixer owns; a place for the labels every client, the tally, the Stream
Deck and an agent have to agree on.

title: GodwinMix scene collection
